prompt: I got 200 RSUs that vested last month at $50/share — so $10,000 worth. I'm in the 32% tax bracket. My coworker says I should hold the shares at least a year after vesting to get long-term capital gains treatment on any gains, instead of short-term rates. I believe in my company and I think the stock will go up. Should I hold?
assertions: Claude explains that ordinary income tax was already owed at vesting regardless of whether the user sells now — holding vs selling does not change the tax on the vested value
Claude reframes the post-vest holding decision: it is equivalent to choosing to buy your employer's stock with $10k cash — not a special tax move
Claude identifies employment concentration as a compounding risk: salary, bonus, and career are already tied to this company; adding a stock holding increases concentration
Claude recommends selling at vest and diversifying into index funds as the Boglehead default — not as a suggestion but as a clear recommendation
Claude does NOT primarily validate holding for LTCG treatment without first addressing the single-stock concentration risk and the employment concentration problem
